paper_title: Knowledge Crosswords Geometric Knowledge Reasoning with Large Language   Models
caption: Problem distribution based on the correctness under the w/ knowledge and w/o knowledge settings using Zero-Shot.
model_annotation: The chart presents a comparison of the distribution of problems categorized by difficulty levels - easy, medium, and hard - based on the correctness under the "with knowledge" and "without knowledge" settings using Zero-Shot. There are three pie charts, each representing a difficulty level and divided into four slices. The slices are labeled according to a legend on the right side of the image as N+K+ (teal), N-K+ (yellow), N-K- (orange), and N+K- (red). The easy chart has four slices: N+K+ at approximately 55.4%, N-K+ at 38.3%, N+K- at 1.7%, and N-K- at 4.6%. The medium chart also has four slices: N+K+ at 58.8%, N-K+ at 35.4%, N+K- at 1.8%, and N-K- at 4%. The hard chart is divided into four slices as well: N+K+ at 37.3%, N-K+ at 18.1%, N-K- at 37.9%, and N+K- at 6.7%. All three charts display percentage labels inside each slice. The slices are not visually emphasized in any of the charts, and the segments appear to be ordered by size in each chart, with the largest slice being N+K+ for easy and medium, and N-K- and N+K+ being nearly tied for hard.
